cards.text: Friend, pull up a stool. Korah, a Levite from the family of Kohath, teams up with three men from the tribe of Reuben: Dathan, Abiram and On. Together they start a rebellion against Moses, Israel's leader.

cards.question: Korah's crew isn't small. How many men of Israel join the rebellion, all known as leaders of the congregation?

cards.text: They come together against Moses and his brother Aaron, the priest. Friend, 250 leaders showing up at once is not a meeting, that's an ambush with name tags.

cards.question: Korah's crew tells Moses and Aaron, "You have taken too much upon yourselves!" What do they say about everyone in the congregation?

answers.text: They're all holy and the LORD is in their midst
They're all worn out from the long wilderness road
They're all ready to choose a brand new leader

cards.question: Then they ask Moses and Aaron, "Why then do you exalt yourselves above the assembly of the LORD?" What's the first thing Moses does when he hears this?

cards.text: Moses has a plan. Tomorrow morning, he tells Korah, the LORD will reveal who belongs to Him and who is holy, and He'll bring that person near to Himself.

cards.question: For the test, Moses tells Korah and all his followers to take ___ and put fire and incense in them in the presence of the LORD.
Moses turns Korah's own line around and tells the sons of Levi that they are the ones who have taken too much upon themselves.

cards.text: Then Moses tells Korah, "Now listen, you sons of Levi!" God already set the Levites apart and brought them near to do the work at the LORD's tabernacle and minister to the congregation.

cards.question: Moses says God already brought the Levites near. What does he say Korah and the Levites are after on top of that?

answers.text: Land of their own as well

cards.question: Moses tells Korah that he and his followers have really conspired against Aaron, not against the LORD.

cards.text: Moses sends for Dathan and Abiram, and their answer is "We will not come!" Friend, that's not turning down an invite, that's tearing it up in front of the mailman.

cards.question: Dathan and Abiram complain about the land Moses brought them up out of. How do they describe that land?

answers.text: A land flowing with milk and honey
A land of chains and hard labor
A land of dust and endless famine

cards.text: Yep, they're calling Egypt a land flowing with milk and honey, and they say Moses brought them out to kill them in the wilderness. That's like me calling the junk drawer a five-star hotel.

cards.question: Dathan and Abiram admit that Moses has at least given them an inheritance of fields and vineyards.

cards.text: Now Moses is very angry. He tells the LORD, "Do not regard their offering."

cards.question: Moses tells the LORD he hasn't taken even one ___ from Dathan and Abiram or mistreated a single one of them.

cards.text: So Moses lays it out for Korah one more time. Tomorrow, everyone appears before the LORD, and each man brings his own censer with incense in it.

cards.question: Aaron sits this test out and lets Korah's crew present their censers before the LORD alone.

cards.text: Each man takes his censer, puts fire and incense in it, and stands with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Korah gathers his whole assembly against them right there.

cards.question: With Korah's whole assembly gathered at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, what appears to the whole congregation?

cards.text: And the LORD tells Moses and Aaron, "Separate yourselves from this congregation so that I may consume them in an instant."

cards.question: When the LORD says He will consume the congregation, Moses and Aaron quietly step away just as they were told.
Facedown, Moses and Aaron ask God: when one man sins, will He be angry with the whole ___?

cards.text: The LORD tells Moses to have the congregation move away from the dwellings of Korah, Dathan and Abiram. Friend, when you hear that, you don't ask how far, you just keep backing up till you bump into somebody's camel.

cards.question: Moses heads over to Dathan and Abiram all by himself.

cards.text: Moses warns the congregation, "Move away now from the tents of these wicked men."

cards.question: Moses also tells the congregation not to touch anything that belongs to these men. What does he say will happen if they do?

answers.text: They'll be unclean for a week
They'll be sent outside the camp

cards.text: So the people move away. Meanwhile Dathan and Abiram come out and stand at the entrances to their tents with their wives and children and infants.
Then Moses says this is how they'll know the LORD sent him. If these men die a natural death, he says, then the LORD has not sent him.

cards.question: Moses says that if the LORD sent him, something unprecedented will happen to these men. What?

answers.text: The earth opens and swallows them
A flood sweeps their tents away

cards.question: As soon as Moses finishes saying all this, the ground beneath Dathan and Abiram splits open.

cards.text: The earth opens its mouth and swallows them and their households, all Korah's men and all their possessions. They go down alive into Sheol, the earth closes over them, and they vanish from the assembly.

cards.question: At their cries, all the people of Israel who were around them ___.

cards.text: They're running and shouting, "The earth may swallow us too!" Friend, I hop everywhere on a gold base, and even I would've found a way to sprint.

cards.question: Meanwhile, the 250 men are still standing there offering the incense. What happens to them?

answers.text: Fire from the LORD consumes them
A plague from the LORD strikes them
They're driven out of the camp

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses about the censers. Eleazar, Aaron's son and a priest, is to pull them out of the flames and scatter the coals far away, because the censers are holy.

cards.question: The censers were presented before the LORD, so they have become holy. What does the LORD say to do with them?

answers.text: Hammer them into sheets for the altar
Bury them far outside the camp
Melt them into a bronze basin

cards.text: So Eleazar has the bronze censers hammered out to overlay the altar, just as the LORD commanded through Moses. Out of the flames and onto the altar, friend, and trust me, I know a little something about a comeback like that.

cards.question: The overlaid altar reminds Israel that no outsider who is not a descendant of ___ should approach to offer incense before the LORD.

cards.text: You'd think after all that, the camp gets real quiet. NOPE, the very next day the whole congregation of Israel grumbles against Moses and Aaron.

cards.question: The whole congregation grumbles against Moses and Aaron. What do they accuse them of?

cards.text: The congregation gathers against them, so Moses and Aaron turn toward the Tent of Meeting. Suddenly the cloud covers it, the glory of the LORD appears, and they go to the front of the Tent.

cards.question: Once again, the LORD tells Moses and Aaron to get away from the congregation so He can consume them in an instant.

cards.text: Moses and Aaron fall facedown. Then Moses tells Aaron to fill his censer with fire from the altar, add incense, and go quickly to the congregation to make atonement for them.

cards.question: Why does Moses tell Aaron to hurry to the congregation with his censer?

answers.text: The fire is spreading through camp
The cloud is about to lift

cards.text: So Aaron takes the censer and RUNS into the middle of the assembly, offering the incense and making atonement for the people. Friend, I've never run a day in my life, I hop, and I'm still on my feet cheering for this man.

cards.question: With the plague spreading through the people, Aaron takes his stand. He stood between the ___ and the ___.
Even with Aaron standing there with his incense, the plague keeps on spreading.
Still, many die from the plague, not counting those who died on account of Korah. How many?

cards.text: Then Aaron returns to Moses at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, since the plague has been halted. And that's where we'll set it down for now, friend, because this story is not done with us yet.

findings.problem: The card calls Aaron Moses' brother and 'the priest.' Numbers 16 doesn't say Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14 does). The card's verses field (Numbers 16:2-3) can't carry that outside reference.
findings.question: The docs say outside facts come 'with their reference,' but a story card cites only the passage verses it tells. How should a story card cite an outside fact, like Aaron being Moses' brother? Should the verses field allow an outside reference, should the reference go in the card text, or should the fact be left out?

findings.problem: The blank's answer, 'congregation,' is already given on the cards just before it. Card 3 quotes 'Separate yourselves from this congregation,' and card 4's question says 'consume the congregation.' The baker is handed the word instead of working it out.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Verse 31 says 'the ground beneath them split open.' The card says it opens beneath Dathan and Abiram. The text leaves open exactly who 'them' is, including whether Korah is among them. The card narrows it.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Verse 34 says the people fled 'saying, "The earth may swallow us too!"' The card says they are 'shouting,' which changes how the text describes their speech.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke calls the censers' fate a comeback like Papa Dorin's own rescue. In the text, the censers of men who died for their sin become a warning sign (16:38, 40), not a restoration. The comparison doesn't match the action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card asks about the LORD's line 'so that I may consume them in an instant,' which first appears in 16:21 and is shown on stop 2, card 3. The card even begins with 'Once again.'

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: The statement says the LORD tells Moses and Aaron. Verse 44 says 'the LORD said to Moses.' Aaron is named as a hearer only in 16:20, not here. The baker is asked to mark True a statement that doesn't match the text.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The right answer depends on who the LORD speaks to, which is in 16:44. The card cites only Numbers 16:45.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower. A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: Blank 1 is 'living' and blank 2 is 'dead.' A baker who swaps them, standing 'between the dead and the living,' means the same thing and could argue they're right, but would be marked wrong.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The 'story isn't over' line ('And that's where we'll set it down for now, friend, because this story is not done with us yet') nearly copies the doc's example ('And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.').

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
